messages:
sasha: Quick follow-up to the routing-policy RFC — I prototyped a smaller surface for 'composable scorers' that might simplify runtime integration and make hot-reload safer.

sasha: TL;DR: split a policy into two halves: a compile-time static scorer (very cheap, precomputed factors) + a tiny runtime multiplier hook for dynamic signals (latency, region probes, tenant SLOs).

sasha: Rationale: most of our cost/affinity heuristics are stable per-route. Recomputing them per-request is wasted work and makes hot-reload tricky. We also want to allow teams to add simple runtime adjustments without shipping a full policy compile.

teju: Curious — what does the runtime hook look like? a WASM function per-tenant? how do we bound cost/latency?

sasha: Example sketch:
```yaml
route_scorer:
  static: path/to/compiled-trie (precomputed weights, penalties)
  dynamic_hook: { type: wasm, entry: score, budget_us: 200 }
```
The hook receives a tiny context (route_id, recent_probe_ms, tenant_slo_bucket) and returns a multiplier in [-2.0, 2.0]. Engine multiplies static_score * clamp(mult, 0.1, 10).

devon: I like the isolation idea. Two questions: (1) how do we keep global determinism for tie-breaking if hooks are non-deterministic? (2) caching — do we cache hook outputs per-probe-window?

sasha: (1) Hooks must be declared 'pure' (no network calls) in the runtime contract. We can lint/verify that at load time for wasm (disallow wasi syscalls). If a hook misbehaves, fallback to a safe multiplier.

sasha: (2) yes — default caching window is 1s keyed by (route_id, tenant_bucket). The hook budget is for cold evals; cached hits are zero-cost.

mike: How will this impact telemetry? We need explainability for customer SLA incidents. If a scorer flips traffic due to hook output, ops needs visibility.

devon: Add structured annotations to trace: static_score, multiplier, norm_score, cache_hit. Also emit reason codes when multiplier clipped. That should make it searchable.

sasha: Agreed — will add a small trace envelope. Also proposal: require hooks to emit a short explain string (<=128 bytes) so we can surface it in trace and evaluations.

teju: Hot-reload safety: if we replace static component, do we recompile and atomically swap both static & hook, or can we roll static while keeping old hook?

sasha: Plan: compile-time produces a versioned artifact bundle {static.bin, hook_manifest}. Deploys are atomic by bundle version. Hooks are separately versioned but must pass interop checks with static state shape. We avoid partial swaps that would change scoring semantics mid-flight.

mike: Any perf numbers? If wasm hook runs on-thread per-request, even 200us p50 multiplies across tokens.

devon: We should measure both p50/p99 and % of requests that hit the cache. My guess: with 1s cache and typical traffic, cache-hit >= 80% and amortized cost ~30us/req. But need benchmarks on gce/gpu host class.

policy-bot: scorer-lint: dynamic_hook budget_us=200 flagged for route 'realtime-translate' — consider lowering to 50us or enabling aggressive caching.

teju: Good catch. For latency-critical routes we should default to budget_us=50 and a stricter clamp. Non-critical routes can opt-in to heavier hooks.

sasha: Implementation notes:
- runtime contract: no syscalls, deterministic math, explicit rand forbidden
- sandbox: wasm jitted with gas/budget enforcement and early exit on overrun
- fallback: if hook fails/timeout -> multiplier=1.0 + emit incident telemetry
- migration: run static-only mode for one week, enable hooks in opt-in stage, then flip default allow

devon: One more: policy rollout testing. We should simulate scoring with offline replay and compare rank shifts. Add a 'rank-delta' metric so PMs know if traffic moved >X%.

sasha: Yep. I'll wire a sim that runs compiled static scorer + hook-sim on historical probes and emits rank deltas. We'll gate rollout by max-rank-delta and p99-latency delta.

mike: Sounds solid. Can you add an ops playbook for 'hook regression' — how to force-disable all hooks cluster-wide?

sasha: I'll add a cluster-level flag (runtime-config: allow_dynamic_hooks=false) that immediately disables and serves cached static scores only. Will also expose per-tenant whitelist in console.

teju: Thanks. LGTM for next-step prototype. Small ask: include a short safety checklist in the PR — perf numbers, lint results, explain telemetry sample.

sasha: Will do. Posting prototype link in a follow-up comment in ~30m. :rocket:
